localeSwitcher.label: Language
fieldHelp.providers: Each enabled provider checks the domain independently; if even one says "block", the quorum blocks (OR logic). More providers means wider coverage, but more third parties see your queries.
fieldHelp.timeoutMode: What to do when a provider doesn't answer in time: let the site open (default), block it, or let it open and mark the decision as incomplete in the log.
fieldHelp.cache: Min/max lifetime of a cache entry (caps the provider's own TTL), how long to keep a "blocked" verdict, and how many entries the cache holds at once before it starts evicting the oldest.
fieldHelp.overrides: Your own exceptions on top of the filters: allowed domains are never blocked, blocked domains are always blocked, whatever the providers say. A domain on both lists is allowed.
fieldHelp.logFilters: Search and filters cover only what the log still keeps (see "Keep the log for").

cctldBlock.heading: Block country domain endings
cctldBlock.description: Blocks every site whose address ends in a chosen country ending (e.g. .ru).
cctldBlock.overBlockingWarning: Blocking a country ending catches every domain under it - regardless of who actually runs the site or where its content is hosted. Many legitimate sites register under an ending that doesn't match their own country (e.g. .io/.co) for reasons unrelated to it.
cctldBlock.inputPlaceholder: Country or ending, e.g. Russia or ru…
geoip.heading: GeoIP block
geoip.intro: Blocks a site whose server address belongs to one of the countries you list here.
geoip.noDatabaseStatus: The GeoIP database isn't loaded yet - country filtering isn't in effect right now, regardless of the list below.
geoip.unknownBuildDateStatus: The GeoIP database is loaded; its build date is unknown.
geoip.overBlockingWarning: Large CDNs (Cloudflare, Google, Amazon) hand out anycast addresses whose apparent geography changes between requests - blocking a country risks blocking legitimate sites that simply route through a data center in that country, with no actual tie to its jurisdiction.

browserSetup.heading: Connect your browser
browserSetup.intro: Enter this address as the "custom DNS provider" in your browser settings:
browserSetup.forOtherBrowser: Couldn't detect the browser - general instructions:
browserSetup.chromium.step1: Open a new tab and paste into the address bar (a web page can't open browser settings pages through a link - paste it by hand):
browserSetup.chromium.step2: "Use secure DNS" → "Custom" → paste the address from above.
browserSetup.edge.step2: Turn on "Use secure DNS" → "Choose a service provider" → paste the address from above.
browserSetup.edge.managedNote: If the switch is greyed out with a briefcase icon, Edge considers itself managed by an organization: this computer has at least one Edge policy (Windows "optimization" tools often leave one behind). The DNS setting then can't be changed in Edge itself; the list of policies is at edge://policy.
browserSetup.brave.step2: "Use secure DNS" is already on → in the provider list choose the option to add a custom provider → paste the address from above.
browserSetup.opera.step2: Turn on "Use DNS-over-HTTPS instead of the system's DNS settings" (Opera picks Cloudflare right away) → choose the last option in the list, the one with no name and a text field → paste the address from above.
browserSetup.vivaldi.step2: Section "DNS over HTTPS" → choose the custom DNS provider option → paste the address from above. A green check mark means Vivaldi accepted the address.
browserSetup.firefox.step1: Open a new tab and paste into the address bar:
browserSetup.firefox.step2: Section "DNS over HTTPS" → "Max Protection" → "Choose provider" → "Custom" → paste the address from above.
browserSetup.firefox.mode2Warning: Choose "Max Protection", not "Increased Protection": with "Increased Protection" Firefox silently falls back to the system DNS on every blocked site - and the site opens.
browserSetup.firefox.librewolf: LibreWolf is not supported: it doesn't trust certificates from the Windows certificate store, so it can't connect to the service.
browserSetup.other.step1: In your browser settings find "DNS over HTTPS" / "Secure DNS" / "Custom DNS provider".
browserSetup.other.step2: Choose the "Custom" mode and paste the address from above.
browserSetup.verify: Check: open any site - it should appear in the log below as Allowed. To confirm that filtering really works, add a test domain to your blocked domains and open it: the browser should show ERR_ADDRESS_INVALID (not ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED).
browserSetup.verifyFirefox: Check: open any site - it should appear in the log below as Allowed. To confirm that filtering really works, add a test domain to your blocked domains and open it: Firefox shows "Hmm. We're having trouble finding that site." and the log shows it as Blocked.
browserSetup.localNetworkNote: If a site asks to access apps and services on this device (local network), choose Block. Otherwise it could read which sites you opened recently from this filter and add fake entries to your log.
danger.heading: Full removal
danger.warning: Stops DNS Quorum Filter and removes everything it left on this computer: the trusted certificate, the stored keys and credentials (TLS key, the log/cache encryption key, the personal-zone key, MaxMind credentials if any) and the whole data folder, then opens Windows Settings so you can remove the app itself. This is the same action as the "Remove everything" item in the tray icon menu; you confirm it in the DNS Quorum Filter window.
danger.requested: Request sent. Confirm the removal in the DNS Quorum Filter window - the app will then close and this page will stop responding.
danger.trayNotRunning: The DNS Quorum Filter tray icon is not running, so there is nowhere to confirm the removal. Start DNS Quorum Filter from the Start menu and press the button again.

blocklist.heading: Public blocklists
blocklist.title: Block using public blocklists
blocklist.desc.off: Adds public block lists (ads, trackers, malware, newly registered and machine-generated domains) on top of the filters. Optional, off by default. Applies before the providers are asked.
blocklist.desc.pipelineNote: Applies before the providers are asked.
blocklist.emptyNotice.active: Turned on, but no source is selected - blocking still applies to the previously loaded set (it isn't cleared automatically until you select a source).
blocklist.emptyNotice.inactive: Turned on, but no source is selected - filtering isn't in effect. Tick at least one source below.
blocklist.forkBNotice: Turned on; the first download is running in the background. Until it finishes nothing extra is blocked - the result shows here when it's done.
blocklist.orphanDesc: unknown source (no longer published) - untick it to save your other changes
blocklist.status.unchecked: unticked - stays in effect until the next refresh
blocklist.source.hageziMultiPro.desc: Ads, trackers, malware - the main set
blocklist.source.adguardDnsFilter.desc: Same class, a separate source - wider coverage
blocklist.source.oneHostsLite.desc: Same again, a lighter list - fewer false blocks
blocklist.source.hageziNrdDga.desc: Newly registered and machine-generated domains (often used to control malware)
